settings.name: Full
settings.text: Banks get the Money Market: their debtors, offices and rival banks in one panel, a map of who owes them, and their own trust and greed. They may also hold land: towns won in wars they pay for, seized pledges and protectorates.

settings.name: Money Only
settings.text: Banks lend, take pledges, sell war bonds, build their standing and face runs, but never hold land: they pay for no wars, keep no merchant towns, seize no pledged places and take no country under their protection.

settings.name: Disabled
settings.text: Banks play as in the base game.

policies.name: Sound Money
policies.text: We lend little and keep coin in the chest. Depositors sleep well.

policies.name: Merchants' Credit
policies.text: We lend to merchants against goods and bills, as the Florentine houses did at every fair.

policies.name: Lending to Princes
policies.text: We lend to kings at high rates. The Bardi and the Peruzzi lent Edward III more than they owned.

laws.name: Interest
laws.text: How the house charges for its money while the Church forbids usury.

policies.name: Exchange Contracts
policies.text: Our interest hides in bills of exchange between one fair and the next. The exchange costs us a little.

policies.name: Discretionary Gifts
policies.text: We charge nothing, and our debtors give us what they think fair. Our name is clean and our income less sure.

policies.name: Open Interest
policies.text: We charge interest openly, as England's act of 1545 allowed and Calvin defended.

laws.name: Partnership
laws.text: Who owns the house and who answers for its debts.

policies.name: Family Company
policies.text: The house belongs to the family and a few trusted partners, each liable to his last florin. Secrets stay in the family.

policies.name: Branch Partnerships
policies.text: Each branch is its own partnership, as the Medici ran theirs. One branch's ruin stops at its own books.

policies.name: Limited Partners
policies.text: Outsiders put money in and answer only for their stake, as Florence allowed from 1408. They want their returns.

policies.name: Family Money
policies.text: We hold the money of the family and its friends, and little else.

policies.name: Time Deposits
policies.text: Depositors leave their money for a term and take a share of the profit. They cannot all come at once.

policies.name: Open Deposits
policies.text: Anyone may leave money with us and take it back on demand, as the depositors of the Bardi and the Peruzzi did in 1343.

privileges.name: Depositors' Charter
privileges.text: The house answers to its depositors before the merchants' court. Their claims are heard first and in full.

privileges.name: Partners' Seats
privileges.text: The outside partners sit at the house's table. Their names open courts, and their voice is louder.

value.text: How much risk the house takes. A Prudent house keeps its depositors calm and its name good, and earns less on its money. A Bold house takes more from every loan, bond and pledge, and every loss shakes it harder.

advances.name: The Accomandita
advances.text: Florence's statute of 1408 lets partners put money into a house and answer only for their stake.

advances.name: Branch Houses
advances.text: From 1397 the Medici made each of their branches a partnership of its own, so that no one branch could sink the house.

advances.name: Lawful Interest
advances.text: England's act of 1545 allowed interest up to ten in the hundred, and Calvin wrote the same year that interest is no sin in itself.

buildings.name: Bank Chapel
buildings.text:
A chapel the bank keeps beside its office, with masses said for the partners' souls and alms given at its door. The town sees the bank's money doing some good.

Once it is finished, our greed falls 2.5 a year faster for 10 years, if fewer than three charities run then. Only where we keep an office, and only while its owner thinks well of us (opinion 100).

buildings.name: Seized Pledge
buildings.text: A place a crown pledged to a bank and failed to redeem. The bank's factors keep its books and take the bank's share of its raw goods profit for good, while the land stays the crown's.

buildings.name: Merchant House
buildings.text:
The bank's house in its merchant town, where its factors keep the town's books and its trade. A share of the town's taxes goes to the bank, and the town grows around it.

Every merchant town is founded with one. Only in a merchant town's capital.

effect_groups.label: In its location, whatever its level

children.text: Is subject type is Merchant Town

buildings.name: Counting House
buildings.text:
Clerks, ledgers and a strongroom behind the bank's office, where letters of exchange are written and local accounts kept. Each level makes the bank stand 15 stronger in this town, and its standing spreads further from here. Each level costs the bank 0.2 gold a month; a bank that cannot pay loses a level where it stands lowest.

Only where we keep an office, and only under a charter from the town's owner (the office itself still needs its owner's opinion of 100).

actions.name: Ask for a Loan
actions.text: Ask a house for a loan. What it cannot lend alone it offers to the other houses as shares, and each house that joins lends its share.

actions.name: Buy Back a Location
actions.text: Pay a bank the worth of a place it holds that was ours: a merchant town or protectorate made from our land, or a pledge it seized in our land. A bank cannot refuse a full price.

actions.name: Lend Against a Pledge
actions.text: Lend a crown gold against one of its places, which pays us a share of its raw goods profit every month.

actions.name: Pay for a Debt War
actions.text: Pay a crown to fight beside us against a crown that expelled our offices or repudiated its debt to us. We declare the war and make its peace.

actions.name: Finance a War
actions.text: Pay a crown to take one province from a neighbour. The province becomes our merchant town.

actions.name: Buy a War Bond
actions.text: Pay a crown at war now. It pays us back when the war ends, with a premium if its side wins.

actions.name: Lead the War
actions.text: Lead a war we paid for and make its peace ourselves.

actions.name: Hide Our War Bond
actions.text: Spend our spies in an enemy of a secret bond so it is less likely to find out.

actions.name: Close Their Offices
actions.text: Pull down a house's offices in our land.

actions.name: Dismiss Our Court Banker
actions.text: We send the bank's men from our court and keep our income for ourselves.

actions.name: Send Agents
actions.text: Our factors settle in a country where we already stand, buying goodwill in its towns.

actions.name: Recall Agents
actions.text: Our factors come home from a country, and we stop paying for them.

actions.name: Fund the City
actions.text: We pave its streets, endow its guilds and raise a loggia in our name.

actions.name: Buy Out Their Loans
actions.text: We buy what a crown owes the other banks, at the debt and a tenth.

actions.name: Undercut Them
actions.text: We pay off what a crown owes the other banks and take its loans over at a lower rate.

actions.name: Spread Rumours
actions.text: Our spies spread doubt about a rival bank wherever both of us do business.

actions.name: Stop the Rumours
actions.text: Our spies stop spreading doubt about a rival bank.

actions.name: Pay Informers
actions.text: We pay clerks and couriers in a rival house to tell us what they see.

actions.name: Stop the Informers
actions.text: We stop paying our informers in a rival house.

actions.name: Buy Out Rival Offices
actions.text: In a town that stands with us, we buy a rival bank's house and close it. No bank sells its house in its own home town.

actions.name: Make Them Our Client
actions.text: We ask a small crown that lives on our credit to become our client.

actions.name: Gift to the Pope
actions.text: A gift to the Holy See, priced like any crown's gift.

actions.name: Fund a Hospital
actions.text: The bank pays for a hospital in one of its office towns. The town's owner owns it and keeps it.

actions.name: Commission a Work of Art
actions.text: The bank pays a painter for a work in one of its office towns. The work stays ours and hangs there.

concepts.name: Bank Standing
concepts.text:
A bank's standing in a Location runs from 0 to 100: how far the town trusts its house. It comes from the bank's buildings there (an office 40, each level of a counting house 15, a chapel 5) and spreads to the places around, losing 25 at each step, half that along a road, more over hills, forests and mountains. Standing that comes in from another country's lands stops at 25 unless the bank keeps a building in that country.

Agents (+10), gifts to the town (+20 for ten years) and the crown's debt to the bank (up to +10) raise it where they are paid for, and do not spread; hatred, a run on the bank and a refused usury charge lower it. It moves 2 a month toward what all this gives. One bank holds a place; another builds its own standing there the same way and takes the place after standing 10 higher for six months.

A country's Hold is its banks' standing averaged over its places.

concepts.name: Hold
concepts.text:
A bank's hold over a country is its Bank Standing averaged over all the country's places, as a country's Control is averaged over its places. A small country is held by building in a few towns; a large one takes many.

The hold sets how the crown deals with the bank: Known from 10 (answers +10), Trusted from 25 (answers +20, more patience before it repudiates, Bank Charter at half price), Court Banker from 50, Master of the Purse from 75.

concepts.name: Court Banker
concepts.text:
One bank at a time sits as a crown's court banker: the one with the highest Hold of 50 or more that keeps an office in the crown's lands. It takes the seat only when the crown's opinion of it is 50 or more, and keeps it while its hold stays at 50 and above every rival's, it keeps an office there and pays its retainer.

The crown answers it 30 better, bears more before it repudiates its loans, never expels it, and answers a rival's charter 50 worse. The bank takes 3% of the crown's income each month and pays a retainer of 2% of it, at least 0.2 gold.

The crown resents the cut. It may dismiss its court banker, who then waits ten years for the seat.

concepts.name: Master of the Purse
concepts.text: A Court Banker whose Hold reaches 75 becomes master of the crown's purse. It takes 5% of the crown's income, the crown goes to war for it without being paid when every other condition holds, and the crown answers other banks' loans 30 worse. The crown resents a master more than a court banker.

concepts.name: Bank Charter
concepts.text:
A crown sells a bank its charter to raise counting houses in its lands, for two months of the crown's income (10 to 300), at half where the bank is Trusted. A bank holds a charter wherever it kept an office at the start. Each counting house level costs the bank 0.2 gold a month.

A crown can take a charter back. An AI crown does so once its opinion of the bank falls below -25, and below -50 it closes its lands to the bank's new buildings.

concepts.name: Client of the House
concepts.text: A bank may take a small country under its wing. It must have held the country at 90 or more for ten years; the country must owe it a year of its income or have defaulted on it, have no allies to defend it and no overlord; and its ruler must agree. A bank keeps one client for every ten offices.

run.name: A Run on the Bank
run.text: Partners and depositors want their money back, all at once. Every month they call a share of what is left, and the lower our trust stands, the more they call.

starts.text: Trust below 40 (5 percent a month; below 20 at once)
No run on this bank in the last 10 years

children.text: Our home city stands behind us

actions.name: Pay Out in Public
actions.text: Pay a tenth of the claims left at the counter, where the whole town can watch.

actions.name: Call in a Loan
actions.text: Call in a debtor's loans. A crown that still thinks well of us and has the gold pays at once. Any other refuses, and the loan is lost.

actions.name: Ask for Surety
actions.text: A crown that owes us favours stands surety for the bank.

actions.name: Hide the Losses
actions.text: Keep the worst of the books out of sight. Trust returns now, and the truth may come out later.

actions.name: Ask Friends to Wait
actions.text: A crown that thinks well of us lets its claims wait.

actions.name: Ask the Home City
actions.text: Ask the holder of our home city to stand behind us.

actions.name: Call on the House
actions.text: We hold our own home city, so our house stands behind us instead: our protectorates, towns and clients.

actions.name: Sell a Pledge
actions.text: Sell a pledge to another bank for 60 percent of its worth.

actions.name: Settle with a Defaulter
actions.text: A crown that repudiated us takes its lost debt back as a long loan at a low rate, as Genoa's bankers settled with Spain.

organisations.name: The Money Market
organisations.text: Who owes the banks, where they keep offices, and how far the world trusts them.

statuses.name: Bank of the Market
statuses.text: Votes by its worth and its buildings, averaged over the years.

statuses.name: Banker of the Fair
statuses.text: One of the five banks with the largest votes. Under the Conto only they vote and lead joint loans, and each pays a hundredth of its worth a year to the other banks.

statuses.name: The Fair's Bank
statuses.text: The leading bank under the Fair's Bank. Trust and the other banks' fees flow to it.

laws.name: Carry-Over Rate
laws.text: The rate banks charge for carrying a debt to the next fair.

policies.name: Each Bank's Own Rate
policies.text: Each bank lends at its own rate.

policies.name: The Fair's Rate
policies.text: Every bank lends at the average of the banks' own rates, set each year. A share of 5 gold is enough to join a joint loan, and banks join one at 40 trust instead of 50.

policies.name: Raised Rate
policies.text: Banks lend a point higher. Greed follows the rate.

laws.name: Crowns That Fail
laws.text: What the banks do when a crown fails to pay them.

policies.name: Each Bank Alone
policies.text: Each bank bears its own loss.

policies.name: Settle Together
policies.text: The bank owed most answers for every bank owed by a bankrupt crown. It offers half of what they lost as 20 year loans at half its rate, or holds out. If it holds out or the crown refuses, no bank lends to that crown for 10 years.

policies.name: Freeze Their Credit
policies.text: A crown that goes bankrupt, repudiates a debt to a bank or refuses a bank's call for its loan gets no loans from any bank for 10 years. No bank may take over its loans either.

laws.name: Seats at the Fair
laws.text: Which banks vote, propose and lead joint loans, and what a seat costs. A bank's vote is its worth and its buildings, averaged over the years. Each building level it owns, at home or abroad, counts 200 gold.

policies.name: Open Fair
policies.text: Every bank votes and proposes.

policies.name: The Conto
policies.text: Only the five banks with the largest votes vote and lead joint loans. Each pays a hundredth of its worth a year, shared equally among the other banks. Every bank may propose.

policies.name: Matriculation
policies.text: A new bank pays a tenth of its worth, at least 100 gold, before it votes or joins joint loans. The fee goes to the other banks by their votes.

laws.name: Sureties
laws.text: What banks must keep against a run.

policies.name: No Sureties
policies.text: Banks keep what they choose.

policies.name: Sureties
policies.text: A tenth of what a bank has lent stays in gold. That gold is not lent, put into pledges, war bonds or wars, or spent buying loans.

policies.name: The Fair's Bank
policies.text: The leading bank gains a point of trust a month up to 90. Every other bank pays it a hundredth of its worth each year. A run on it costs every other bank 10 trust.

policies.name: No Ceiling
policies.text: Banks charge what they like. The Church charges a greedy Catholic bank for usury.

policies.name: Ceiling at 8%
policies.text: No bank lends above 8%, and a loan a bank takes over falls to 8%. Greed raises hatred to seven tenths of its usual level, and the Church charges no usury.

policies.name: Pawn Banks
policies.text: Each Catholic bank pays a fiftieth of its worth a year to pawn banks for the poor. Hatred fades half a point a month faster in its towns, and Catholic crowns hosting its offices think better of it each year.

laws.name: War Lending
laws.text: How banks may fund crowns at war.

policies.name: Free War Lending
policies.text: Banks fund any war and buy any war bond.

policies.name: No Bank Against Another
policies.text: No bank funds a war or buys a war bond against a crown another bank is funding.

policies.name: Joint War Loans Only
policies.text: Banks fund no wars, buy no war bonds and take no pledges from a crown at war. A crown at war borrows only by joint loan, and the bank it asks lends at most half.

laws.name: Dealing Between Banks
laws.text: What banks may do to each other.

policies.name: Open Rivalry
policies.text: Banks buy each other's loans, undercut each other and spread rumours.

policies.name: Fair Dealing
policies.text: No undercutting and no rumours. Loans are bought only at full price.

policies.name: Closed Books
policies.text: No bank buys another's loans, undercuts or spreads rumours.

organisations.name: House of the Bank
organisations.text: The countries under a bank's wing: its protectorates, its merchant towns and its clients. The bank alone sets the house's laws, and every member pays it a tribute from its income.

statuses.name: Favoured
statuses.text: A member the bank favours: it is more loyal and pays half its tribute. A bank favours two members at most.

laws.name: Tribute
laws.text: How much of their income the members pay the bank.

policies.name: Light Tribute
policies.text: Each member pays 5% of its income. They are grateful for it.

policies.name: Customary Tribute
policies.text: Each member pays 10% of its income, as is the custom.

policies.name: Heavy Tribute
policies.text: Each member pays 15% of its income, and resents it.

laws.name: Defence
laws.text: Who pays for the members' garrisons.

policies.name: The House Keeps the Garrisons
policies.text: The bank pays each member 3% of its income for its garrisons. The members are more loyal for it.

policies.name: Each Keeps Its Own
policies.text: Every member pays for its own garrisons.

laws.name: Government
laws.text: How the bank rules its members.

policies.name: The Councils Keep Their Charters
policies.text: The members govern themselves under their old charters. Their tribute is 2 points of their income lower, and they are more loyal.

policies.name: The House Sends Governors
policies.text: The bank's governors sit in the members' councils. Their tribute is 5 points of their income higher, and they resent it.

payments.name: Tribute to the House
payments.text: Every member pays the bank a share of its income from trade and taxes, set by the house's laws.

payments.name: Garrison Pay
payments.text: The bank pays each member a share of its income to keep its garrisons.

subjects.name: Merchant Town
subjects.text: A town of one province under a bank. It cannot be annexed and makes no wars of its own.

subjects.name: Client of the House
subjects.text: A small country that lives on a bank's credit and follows its lead. It cannot be annexed and makes no wars of its own.

subjects.name: Protectorate of the House
subjects.text: A country under a bank's protection. It keeps its own government and ruler, pays the house its tribute, makes no wars of its own and stands with the bank in defence. It cannot be annexed.

actions.name: Favour a Member of the House
actions.text: We favour a member of our house: it pays half its tribute and is more loyal. We favour two at most.

actions.name: Withdraw a Favour
actions.text: We withdraw our favour from a member of our house: it pays its full tribute again.

actions.name: Entrust a Place to the Bank
actions.text: We hand one of our provinces to a bank we owe at least a year of our income. It becomes a country of its own under the bank's protection, and our debt to the bank falls by the province's worth.

actions.name: Ask for a Place
actions.text: Ask a crown with a debt to us of a year of its income for one of its provinces. It becomes our protectorate, and the crown's debt falls by the province's worth.

countries.country: Most Serene Republic of Saint George
countries.text: The Protectors of the Casa take the city that made them. Liguria becomes ours and the bank a republic. If Genoa itself still holds the city, the rest of Genoa becomes our protectorates.
countries.result: We ask the ruler of Genoa to give the city to the Casa. If it agrees, we take Liguria and become the Most Serene Republic of Saint George, and its debts to us are settled. If that ruler is Genoa itself, Genoa ends: its subjects ruled by the AI and its lands abroad become our protectorates (one for each area of its land), and a subject ruled by a player goes free. We remain a bank: our offices, loans, standing and house stay ours. Land beyond our seat's ten places lowers the trust our books allow, a war we declare costs trust each month, and our enemies may repudiate what they owe us.
requirements: No person plays the ruler of the city of Genoa
We are master of the purse to the ruler of Genoa
We sit as court banker to Castile or Spain
We keep offices in Seville and Antwerp
We keep an office at the exchange fair, in Besancon or Piacenza
We have held a protectorate for 25 years
We have weathered a run on our doors
No run is on, and we are at peace

countries.text: Our loans bought Corinth and our hired lances took Athens. The King of Naples gives it a lawful duke from our family.
countries.result: Our subject that holds Athens becomes the Duchy of Athens, taking its name and arms if it is not the Duchy already. An Acciaioli becomes its duke. Our other subjects' places in the province of Corinth pass to it. It is no longer our subject, and we become its state bank. We remain a bank. If we are played, we choose to rule Athens or stay the bank. This happens once in a game.
requirements: One of our subjects holds a place in the province of Corinth, or a place there is pledged to us
One of our subjects holds Athens
No person plays the ruler of Athens
We sit as court banker to the ruler of Naples
No run is on, and we are at peace

countries.text: Joseph Nasi stood at the sultan's side and lent to his court. Selim II made him Duke of Naxos and the Cyclades.
countries.result: We ask the ruler of Constantinople for Naxos. If it agrees, the islands of the province of Naxos become the Duchy of the Archipelago, its tributary, taking the Duchy's name and arms if they are not the Duchy already. A duke of our family rules them, and we become the Duchy's state bank. We remain a bank. If we are played, we choose to rule Naxos or stay the bank. This happens once in a game.
requirements: We keep an office in Antwerp, in Venice and in Constantinople
We sit as court banker to the ruler of Constantinople
The ruler of Constantinople, or one of its subjects, holds Naxos
No person plays the ruler of Constantinople or of Naxos
No run is on, and we are at peace

countries.text: The Emperor owes us for his wars and his election. He pledged us Kirchberg and Weissenhorn, and a Fugger can sit among the counts of the Empire.
countries.result: Our subject in the province of Augsburg becomes the County of Kirchberg and Weissenhorn and a member of the Empire. A Fugger becomes its count. Our other subjects' places in that province pass to it. It is no longer our subject, and we become its state bank. We remain a bank. If we are played, we choose to rule the county or stay the bank. This happens once in a game.
requirements: A place in the province of Schwaz is pledged to us, or one of our subjects holds it
One of our subjects holds a place in the province of Augsburg
We sit as court banker to the Emperor
No person plays our subjects in the province of Augsburg
No run is on, and we are at peace
